newsitem.title: USA: California measures set standards on cheap pistols.
newsitem.headline: California measures set standards on cheap pistols.

text.p: Gun control lobbyists hailed on Thursday a pair of bills passed by the California legislature intended to ban the sale and manufacture of pistols known as "Saturday night specials" in the state.

The measures must be reconciled into one bill and then signed by Gov. Pete Wilson. Wilson has not indicated whether he would sign a bill but his spokesman, Sean Walsh, said the governor believed individuals, particularly women, had a right to possess guns for self-protection and was concerned that handguns meeting the new requirements would be too expensive for low-income women.

The cheap pistols are a favourite of criminals because they sell on the street for as little as $50. Some experts estimate 70 percent of gun-related crimes in the United States involve Saturday night specials.

The regulations, which would be phased in beginning in October and be in full effect by next June 1, would require all handguns sold in California to include child-proofing features, tamper-proof serial numbers and detailed consumer safety warnings.
California produces about 700,000 of the cheap handguns a year, the vast majority of the nation's supply, according to Handgun Control, a lobby group.
The California bills would prohibit the sale of the pistols by individuals or manufacturers but it would not ban people already owning the handguns from keeping them.
Both bills require all handguns manufactured in the state to meet established federal standards that govern the quality of the metal used in the guns and whether the guns can discharge when dropped.

The federal standards were set in 1968 after Sen. Robert Kennedy was killed by an assassin using an imported Saturday night special. The law banned the importation of such weapons but allowed U.S. companies to continue manufacturing them.
